A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LumiNet, with matching core equations and retained benchmark results. Text, tables, figures, and equations are readable throughout. The supplied v2 ends with references; v3 includes Appendices A.1–A.17. Newly supplied details are not automatically treated as newly introduced procedures.

before.justification: V2 reports original classification, detection, transfer-learning, and ablation results in Tables 1–6 and Figure 4.

after.justification: V3 retains original vision results and reports additional NLP, calibration, label-noise, and optimization experiments in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The core batchwise normalization and KL distillation remain unchanged. V3 adds the Ours++ variant using global teacher statistics (A.13) and tests a dual-focal-loss combination (Table 5). Explicitly documenting cross-entropy alongside distillation does not establish that cross-entropy was newly added to the original procedure.

E1.justification: V3 retains the four vision datasets and substantially extends coverage to GLUE language-understanding tasks and language-model evaluation on Dolly, SelfInst, and Vicuna. It also evaluates CIFAR-100 under instance-dependent label noise (A.11).

E2.justification: V3 adds BDCKD and TTM to the existing CIFAR-100 comparison, PD/PKD/TinyBERT/CKD/MGSKD to GLUE comparisons, KD+FL/KD+DFL/FCUC to calibration comparisons, and SeqKD to language-model comparisons. These are reported comparator entries, not merely additional citations.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include 15-bin ECE/MCE and classwise FPR95, constructed label-noise training, batch sizes 4/64/256, and NLP development/test protocols. ImageNet settings also become inconsistent: v3 A.9 states batch size 512 and learning rate 0.2, while both main texts state 128 and 0.1. This reporting difference does not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V3 adds difficult-class error analysis, calibration comparisons, gradient/entropy/convergence analyses, prediction-similarity heatmaps, noisy-supervision robustness, very-small-batch sensitivity, global-versus-local statistics, and architecture-misalignment analysis. The earlier temperature, ensemble, batch-size, and transfer-learning analyses are largely retained in A.2 and Figure 3 rather than removed.

E5.justification: V3 Table 1 first specifies five trials and supplies standard deviations for LumiNet across the CIFAR-100 model pairs. Table 15 specifies averages over five random seeds. V2 provides no corresponding run counts or dispersion reporting; this establishes expanded reporting, not an explicit increase in previously performed runs.

E6.justification: Original benchmark means are largely retained, including ImageNet Top-1 scores of 72.16 and 72.55. V3 adds extensive results for new comparators, NLP, calibration, robustness, and method variants. For example, Table 13 reports noisy-setting accuracy of 54.70 versus KD's 53.88, and Table 15 reports Dolly scores of 27.8 versus 25.0 for 340M students. These are newly reported comparisons.

T1.justification: V2 mainly supplies the normalization and distillation formulation. V3 adds gradient-preconditioning reasoning and three theorems with proof sketches concerning mutual information, convergence under Lipschitz/Polyak–Łojasiewicz assumptions, and batch-size invariance (A.4–A.7). This substantially expands the formal mathematical content.

C1.justification: V3 adds central claims about suppressing confirmation bias and addressing teacher–student capacity mismatch, and extends applicability claims to NLP. The contribution framing shifts from v2's claim of obsoleting dark knowledge toward statistical calibration and contextual knowledge transfer. The abstract's headline ImageNet gains remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V3 introduces substantive interpretations involving error propagation, gradient stabilization, local-statistics regularization, and architectural misalignment. It adds limitations concerning very small or insufficiently diverse batches, tasks requiring intermediate features, and sensitive information leaking through output logits. V2 primarily discusses granularity, temperature sensitivity, and efficiency.

D1.justification: V3 supplies optimizer settings, training schedules, regularization, ViT configuration, calibration implementation, noise construction, and language-model sample counts and GPU details. It explicitly documents the combined training objective and numerical stabilization. Much of this expands documentation of existing experiments. Conversely, v2's code/model-availability link disappears.

R1.justification: V3 substantially expands positioning through calibration, NLP distillation, normalization, information theory, and optimization literature. It explicitly distinguishes LumiNet from TTM and RKD and connects it to statistical distillation and neural collapse. The perception motivation changes from Johnson's general discussion to Lindorfer's treatment of Lewin's field theory.

P1.justification: The title, introduction, and methodology are extensively rewritten. V2's 'bright side' exposition is reorganized, its main-text ablation section moves into the appendix, and v3 introduces dedicated confirmation-bias/calibration and discussion sections plus a structured appendix. These changes substantially alter the narrative organization.

P2.justification: V3 merges the opening performance and perception illustrations into Figure 1, replacing the Possum example with Sweet Peppers. The old Figure 4 moves to appendix Figure 3. Detection and efficiency tables are combined and reformatted, while new result tables, heatmaps, and training curves substantially expand the visual presentation under a different journal layout.

improvement.justification: V3 strengthens empirical support through calibration/noise tests, NLP coverage, uncertainty reporting, and implementation details. However, new reliability problems offset these benefits: Theorem 1 guarantees positive information gain even though its assumptions allow logits independent of labels, A.5 ignores derivatives through batch statistics, ImageNet settings conflict internally, and Figure 8's curves oppose its caption's stated trend. The substantial documentation gains and newly introduced scientific inconsistencies prevent a confident net-quality judgment.
